conclusions: No within-game raw id or game_play_number duplicates occur in any of the seven pinned assets. The proposed raw-ID collision explanation is unsupported.
All detected duplicate-identity intersections are sequenceNumber-only. In 2025, 414 affected games contain 72693 rows; 4290 repeated sequence groups contain 8813 rows (4523 excess keys).
The (game_id,sequenceNumber,game_play_number) composite is unique in all seven seasons, but uniqueness does not establish chronology.

Sequence and processed play-number order disagree even in games without sequence ties. The four identity-selected examples favor retaining sequence as the primary ordering field, while demonstrating that neither field guarantees chronology.

A conservative local correction can retain sequence order, preserve tied records as barriers, exclude tied rows and their first successor state, and require consecutive game_play_number values on every admitted predecessor/state or clock edge. It must not bridge ties, guess tie order, or treat global field disagreement as proof that every local segment is invalid.
No parser, acquisition receipt, source inventory, frozen plan or previous build was changed by this diagnostic. Coverage repair is a source-semantic decision made before evaluating model performance.

definitions.duplicate_by_field: Within-game duplicate non-null values; rows_in_affected_games counts every raw record in the affected games.
definitions.intersection_profiles: Mutually exclusive game sets showing exactly which fields duplicate.
definitions.numeric_pattern: For positive raw IDs above 2^53, count divisibility by 2^(bit_length(id)-53), the binary64 integer spacing at that magnitude. This is only a numeric pattern, not a proven conversion history.
definitions.ordering: Sort by sequenceNumber, breaking equal sequence ties by game_play_number; detect non-increasing play number. Unique-order conflicts are separately restricted to games with both order fields unique.

fixed_chronology_sample.limits: Four identity-selected games only; clock increases can also reflect official corrections, so no automatic chronology repair is inferred.
fixed_chronology_sample.selection: Two smallest 2025 game IDs with duplicate sequenceNumber; two smallest with unique sequenceNumber and non-increasing game_play_number when sorted by sequenceNumber. Chosen only from identity columns before reading period/clock/type.

limitations: Quarter/clock comparisons cover only the four fixed identity-selected 2025 games and are not a whole-archive chronology certification.
Clock increases can reflect source corrections or administrative record timing; they identify disagreement rather than prove a universal sorting rule.
Original source sequence values are supplied by the upstream feed; the inspected processing code does not independently reconstruct their semantic truth.
Raw IDs above binary64 exact-integer range are retained as nullable Int64. No within-game collision occurs here; the cause of repeated sequence numbers is not established.

publisher_version_limitation: These are the primary publisher code locations inspected during this audit. The exact processor commit and environment that produced each downloaded season asset have not been certified. Mutable main links and source conventions are not a provenance proof for the exact artifacts.
scope: Source-semantic diagnosis before matchup prediction or performance evaluation. Read five identity/order columns in all seven pinned seasons; additionally read period, clock and play type only for the four games selected deterministically using identity properties. No scores, final totals, outcomes, fitted models or performance metrics were inspected.

source_evidence.finding: Official release describes raw per-game JSON capture, processing and publication repositories.
Inspected _sort_plays_ot_aware sorts regulation by id and start.adj_TimeSecsRem; overtime is sorted by sequenceNumber.
Inspected processor casts supplied id and sequenceNumber and applies its sorting helper.
Inspected processor assigns game_play_number with a one-based row index after the preceding sort/filter operations.
Later sorting, deduplication and marker filtering can leave gaps in the already assigned play number.
Inspected publication script flattens supplied play records and conforms schema; it does not establish an independent chronological definition.
